title: Words That Could Not Be Ignored

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: These are the commandments the Lord proclaimed in a loud voice to your whole assembly there on the mountain from out of the fire, the cloud and the deep darkness; and he added nothing more. Then he wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me. - Deut 5:22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses underlines something important about the Ten Commandments: God spoke them directly, "in a loud voice," to the whole assembly. These were not Moses' ideas or a committee's decision. They came from the mouth of God Himself, out of the fire and thick darkness, and then He wrote them with His own hand on stone. And notice the phrase "he added nothing more" — these ten words stood as the foundational summary of the covenant, complete and authoritative.

There is weight here. God's commands are not human suggestions we can negotiate or edit to taste. They flow from His holy character and carry His full authority. In an age when many treat morality as a matter of personal preference, this reminds us that right and wrong are not ours to invent. They are rooted in the very nature of God.

Yet the same God who thundered from the mountain has now spoken most clearly through His Son (Heb 1:1-2). The law written on stone revealed God's will but could not change the human heart. Under the new covenant, God promises to write His law not on tablets but on our hearts (Heb 8:10). What Sinai could command, the Spirit now empowers. The God who spoke with a loud voice still speaks — and through Christ, He writes His ways within us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I treat God's commands as His authoritative voice, or as suggestions I can edit?
- How does it change things to know God's law flows from His holy character?
- What does it mean that God now writes His law on my heart, not just on stone?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You spoke Your commands with authority, for they flow from Your holy character. Thank You that through Christ You now write Your ways on my heart. Give me a heart eager to hear and obey Your voice. Amen.
